questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: They make it harder to control the motorcycle and should be avoided.
They help other drivers see you.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves help you grip the handlebars better. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, what is the safe following distance behind another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance behind another vehicle when riding normally. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one area of the lane and limits your movement.
It lets you rely on others to spot hazards.
It requires you to go faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle helps you have time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night to help other drivers see you. Bright colors with reflective materials make you more visible.

questions.question: Where can you find the best information about your specific motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle
A television show about motorcycle riding

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of these do you NOT need to check before riding?

options.text: Testing the brakes to make sure the brake light works
Checking that the paint is not scratched

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking that the paint is not scratched
questions.explanation: Before riding, check the tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and make sure all lights work properly including headlights, taillights, turn signals, and brake lights.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely
Clothing that covers your arms completely but leaves your legs exposed
Clothing that covers your legs completely but leaves your arms exposed
Whatever makes you most comfortable, regardless of safety

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing that covers your arms and legs completely
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs for proper protection.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on your motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single most effective way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves for safety.

questions.question: How much alcohol does the body get rid of per hour?
questions.explanation: On average, your body can eliminate the alcohol in about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Your body gets rid of about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals about 4 drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make the danger worse by making them tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Do not carry a passenger unless your motorcycle has a seat large enough for two riders. The motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you wear.

questions.question: Which of these is a reason to end a motorcycle skills test?
questions.explanation: The test stops if you drop or fall off the motorcycle, tip or lose control, stall the engine four or more times, do something unsafe, disregard instructions, break a traffic law, or get enough points to fail.

questions.question: Waiting one hour to ride after one drink:

options.text: Guarantees you will not be arrested for drinking and riding.
Guarantees your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average. The time needed varies from person to person. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, you should ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It increases your line of sight.
It decreases your line of sight.
It makes it hard to see beyond the vehicle.
It allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases your line of sight.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing to see better and to be more visible to drivers already passing.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can slow down by downshifting. Remember that downshifting does not turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower it. These things may keep you awake, but they do not make you sober.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than their side mirrors, so this position is safer for you.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is okay as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is okay as long as no other vehicles are nearby.
Can cause you to drift into another lane or off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to drift into another lane or off the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. If you cannot hold the turn, you may drift into another lane or leave the road. Always use caution when turning.

questions.question: What should you NOT check on your tires?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check tire flexibility.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle can cause serious accidents. Inspect your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface on the road?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise off the seat slightly to let your legs absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat slightly to let your legs absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down as much as possible. Keep your motorcycle upright and rise slightly off the seat so your knees can absorb some of the shock. Just before impact, gently roll on the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a motorcycle accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce the risk of injury or death in a motorcycle accident.

questions.question: Are helmets required for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Only for operators with less than one year of experience.

questions.explanation: In Maryland, all motorcycle riders must wear a helmet that meets federal safety standards. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.
